description: Knowledge served through MCP: kb_list and kb_read, deterministic. Kinds by id prefix. tools-: 'modes' (and 'limits') give the tools' names and input schemas. args-: a tool's 'arguments' are validated against 'modes' and 'limits'; expect the arguments with defaults, or an error class. list-, read-, plain-, envsubst-, mustache-, template-: a 'tool' call on 'overlays' (identity, manifest, tree as digest.json writes it, 'served', and the template 'facts' the consumer holds for it: root, state, scope, project and the user's options), with 'arguments', optional 'modes', 'limits' and the caller's 'facts' (caller, env, env_allow); expect the result or an error class. envelope-: a handler's outcome as MCP's tools/call result. plan-: whether an overlay's rules and context are left out of the context because they are served.

What is knowledge: the files under kb/, flows/, references/, rules/ and context/, CONTEXT.md and the files rules and context name; not another file, not a manifest, not an excluded name. Each is listed with its lines and bytes, in path-byte order.
A server that searches says which modes, in the canonical order.
A server with no search lists no 'search'.
'served' is the consumer's own answer: this overlay's rules and context are left out of the context.
A line ends at LF (CR before it dropped); no line after a final LF; an empty file has none; a lone CR ends nothing; a file with no final LF has the line it ends on.
Paths are ordered by their UTF-8 bytes, which is not UTF-16 order: U+FB01 (EF AC 81) before U+1F600 (F0 9F 98 80) in both, but e-acute (C3 A9) after z, and an upper-case path before a lower-case one.

A file of the set that is not served is listed apart with its reason: not UTF-8, larger than max_file_bytes, a name that holds a hiding character, a template of an engine no edition defines (and 'template: true', which names none).
A template is listed with its engine and no lines or bytes, since the text it serves depends on the call; a file with front matter and no template is a plain file.
A link, a special file and a directory are not listed or skipped; they are no file of the set.
A skipped name is shown with its hiding characters written out.
'overlay' limits the answer to one overlay.
Overlays come in the order the consumer gives them, which is composition order.
An overlay is named as an identity is compared: normalized.
An overlay the session does not have.
A session with no overlay lists none.
An argument the tool does not define.
Without from and to, the whole file, joined by LF with no final one.

A file with no template field is served byte for byte: ${...} and {{...}} stay as written, whatever names they hold.
A file whose front matter does not mark a template keeps that front matter in what is served, and its placeholders are not replaced.
Front matter that does not parse makes the file no template: it is served as it is.
A block with no closing fence is no front matter: the file is plain, whatever it says.
A context given for a plain file changes nothing.

Every name an envsubst file reads: the five AOS_ names, the caller's role and profile, the allowed variables of the environment, the call's context (strings, integers and booleans, not a list), and the options. The front matter is dropped; a name with no value, a variable not allowed, an option with a default, a sensitive option, an unknown name, an escape and a Mustache tag are left as written or replaced as the rules say.
A consumer with no caller facts, no environment and no context gives no value: every name is left as written.
Lines count in what is served: the front matter is not part of it, so line 1 is the first line of the body.
A sensitive variable is never given, though the user allowed it: HOME is on the security section's list, SHELL_X and USER are not.
A variable the user did not allow is not given, though the environment has it.
A value is inserted as it is and never read again: a ${...} in a context value stays text.
A configured option of the wrong type.
A rendered text past max_rendered_bytes is refused, never cut.
A range of a rendered file.

Every root a Mustache file reads: overlay, project, caller, env (the allowed ones), options and context. Sections walk lists and take an object as their context; a missing name is empty; a section on a missing or false name is skipped and an inverted one is shown; a comment alone on a line (white space around it allowed) leaves no line, as do section tags alone on theirs; a value is inserted as it is, with no escaping, however it is written; ${...} is plain text here.
